title: The Asset of Vienna
premise: Sebastian Lockridge's Vienna safe house is listed for sale online, and the listing photos reveal documents that three governments will kill to bury: proof of a covert program trading intelligence for political leverage. When the realtor who took the photos is assassinated, Sebastian realizes he was never guarding clients — he was guarding evidence, and his employers have been rewriting his rules to keep him blind. Hunted by an assassin who knows his protocols better than he does, and betrayed by the handler who trained him, Sebastian must smuggle the truth across borders with a defector analyst, Mara Voss, whose own identity was manufactured by the same program. In the end, Sebastian chooses exposure over survival, releasing the files at a diplomatic summit in Vienna and accepting arrest — alive, but stripped of the identity he built, having learned that the price of surviving the system is becoming someone new.
about_author: Ada Joubert is a former risk consultant who spent a decade advising security firms across Central Europe before turning to fiction. She writes from a farmhouse in Slovenia, where she insists her neighbors' theories about local politics are better than any briefing she ever received.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Sebastian Lockridge, POV. A routine rotation check reveals the safe house listed on a Viennese property site, interior photos showing classified documents on a desk. His calls to command go unanswered. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Rules
chapters.summary: Flashback-woven chapter establishing Sebastian's history: recruited after a military scandal, taught that rules are rewritten by whoever holds the file. He photographs the listing himself as insurance. Emotional beat: uneasy loyalty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Realtor Who Knew Too Much
chapters.summary: Sebastian tracks down Petra Lang, the realtor, POV alternating briefly to hers. She admits she was paid anonymously to stage the shoot. That night her apartment burns. Emotional beat: guilt igniting into urgency.

chapters.title: Burn Notice at Dawn
chapters.summary: Sebastian's credentials are revoked mid-mission; his bank accounts freeze. Someone inside has marked him disposable. He goes dark with a go-bag and the one thing they can't freeze: what he knows. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Mara Voss
chapters.summary: Mara Voss, POV. An analyst at the program's Vienna annex notices the same listing and realizes her cover identity appears in the photos' metadata. She runs before her own burn order lands. Emotional beat: terror mixed with grim vindication.

chapters.title: Two Fugitives, One Tram
chapters.summary: Sebastian and Mara collide at a Stephansplatz tram stop, each tailing the same courier. Suspicion gives way to a wary alliance when the courier is killed by a suppressed shot neither heard. Emotional beat: reluctant trust.

chapters.title: The Assassin Called Wren
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. The program's cleaner reviews Sebastian's file and finds gaps — someone edited his history too. Wren begins hunting not just targets but the truth of her own orders. Emotional beat: professional detachment fraying.

chapters.title: Safe House Number Four
chapters.summary: The pair holes up in a decommissioned fallback site Sebastian memorized years ago. They decrypt the photographed documents: Operation LEDGERLINE, trading intelligence for political leverage across three governments. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Rules Rewritten
chapters.summary: Program director Aldous Rehm, POV, learns the asset and the analyst are loose. He orders containment, not capture — dead men keep secrets. Emotional beat: chilling bureaucratic calm masking panic.

chapters.title: The Handler
chapters.summary: Sebastian contacts his old handler, Colin Marsh, in Bratislava, hoping for an ally. Marsh feeds him a route — straight into a trap. Sebastian escapes on instinct alone. Emotional beat: the father-figure myth dying hard.

chapters.title: What Mara Buried
chapters.summary: Mara confesses she helped design LEDGERLINE's data architecture years ago under another name; her identity was rebuilt to hide it. Sebastian must decide if she's a partner or a liability. Emotional beat: raw honesty as survival strategy.

chapters.title: Wren Closes In
chapters.summary: Wren, POV, reconstructs their movements through transit cameras and corners them at a Danube fuel depot. A brutal close-quarters fight; both fugitives escape wounded, Wren deliberately lets them. Emotional beat: doubt taking root in the hunter.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One File
chapters.summary: A tense interlude mapping the stakes: an American senator, a German minister, and an Austrian spymaster all appear in LEDGERLINE. Exposing it could topple coalitions — or be buried forever. Emotional beat: vertigo of scale.

chapters.title: The Journalist's Price
chapters.summary: They approach investigative reporter Tomas Brandt, who demands verification before risking his neck. His newsroom is raided hours later; he barely escapes with his archive. Emotional beat: hope learning its cost.

chapters.title: Ghosts in the Metadata
chapters.summary: Mara discovers a second copy of the full LEDGERLINE archive hidden in a server farm outside Linz — placed there by her former self as insurance. Retrieval means walking into a known location. Emotional beat: confronting who she used to be.

chapters.title: Linz, After Midnight
chapters.summary: The server-farm infiltration. Sebastian draws guards while Mara pulls the drive; a silent alarm trips. They escape through cooling tunnels as the facility burns behind them. Emotional beat: adrenaline giving way to grief for the lives this ends.

chapters.title: Rehm's Ledger
chapters.summary: Rehm, POV, realizes the archive is complete and pivots to diplomacy: offering the senator a scapegoat package with Sebastian's name on it. Emotional beat: power corrupting in real time, elegantly.

chapters.title: The Senator's Offer
chapters.summary: Senator Hale contacts Sebastian directly through a cutout: immunity in exchange for silence and testimony against Rehm only. Sebastian sees the trap — survive by becoming the lie. Emotional beat: temptation met with clarity.

chapters.title: Wren's File
chapters.summary: Wren, POV, pulls her own recruitment records and finds she was orphaned by an earlier iteration of the program. Her handlers made her; now they've ordered her final contract. Emotional beat: rage finding a direction.

chapters.title: An Assassin Defects
chapters.summary: Wren intercepts the fugitives — and instead of killing them, hands over Rehm's movement schedule. Trust is tested brutally; Mara votes no, Sebastian gambles yes. Emotional beat: dangerous alliance forged in shared damage.

chapters.title: The Summit in Vienna
chapters.summary: A closed-door counterterrorism summit convenes at the Hofburg in nine days — the only room where all three governments sit together and the file could land publicly. The plan crystallizes. Emotional beat: purpose replacing flight.

chapters.title: Marsh's Redemption
chapters.summary: Marsh, guilt-ridden, surfaces with Rehm's contingency plan: blame the leak on Mara, stage her death abroad. He offers himself as bait. Emotional beat: a traitor buying back his soul at face value.

chapters.title: Bait in Bratislava
chapters.summary: The decoy operation. Marsh draws the cleanup team while the others move; he is captured, not killed. Sebastian hears him resist interrogation over an open line. Emotional beat: sacrifice without absolution.

chapters.title: Cracks in the Plan
chapters.summary: Brandt's verification hits a snag — one document is forged, planted to discredit everything. Mara must prove which records are genuine using only her memory of the architecture. Emotional beat: pressure threatening to fracture trust.

chapters.title: The Memory Palace
chapters.summary: Mara reconstructs LEDGERLINE's authentication scheme from memory over a sleepless night, validating the core files. Sebastian watches her rebuild herself in the process. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed through work.

chapters.title: Rehm's Counterstroke
chapters.summary: Rehm, POV, leaks a doctored video framing Sebastian as a rogue operative selling state secrets. International manhunt intensifies; allies scatter. Emotional beat: the machinery of narrative as a weapon.

chapters.title: Hunted in the Innere Stadt
chapters.summary: A near-capture in Vienna's first district; Wren covers their extraction, wounding a former colleague. Sebastian confronts what he's asking people to die for. Emotional beat: weight of leadership he never wanted.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Quiet chapter: in a cellar safehouse, the three reckon with what survival has cost — Marsh captured, careers burned, names erased. Sebastian admits he no longer knows who he is without the rules. Emotional beat: stillness before the storm.

chapters.title: Infiltrating the Hofburg
chapters.summary: Using Wren's knowledge of summit security rotations, they map entry through service tunnels and a catering contractor. Every step assumes betrayal. Emotional beat: controlled fear, precision as courage.

chapters.title: The Day Before
chapters.summary: Final preparations; Brandt schedules publication for the moment the file lands. Rehm, POV, senses the trap but proceeds anyway — controlling the story matters more than safety. Emotional beat: two opponents mirroring each other's obsession.

chapters.title: Summit Morning
chapters.summary: The team splits: Mara to the network room, Sebastian to the hall, Wren watching the exits. Marsh, transported as a witness, signals a warning from custody. Emotional beat: coiled anticipation.

chapters.title: The Handoff
chapters.summary: Sebastian reaches a delegate's aide willing to receive the drive — then discovers the aide is Rehm's plant. Ambush in the service corridor; Sebastian fights through, wounded. Emotional beat: betrayal at the threshold.

chapters.title: Mara's Choice
chapters.summary: Mara reaches the network hub but must choose between uploading the archive or extracting proof of her original identity first. She uploads everything, including herself. Emotional beat: self-erasure as an act of integrity.

chapters.title: Lights On
chapters.summary: LEDGERLINE floods every screen at the Hofburg mid-session; Brandt publishes simultaneously. Delegations erupt. Rehm moves calmly for the exit — into Wren. Emotional beat: catharsis at maximum volume.

chapters.title: Rehm and Wren
chapters.summary: Confrontation between maker and instrument. Wren chooses arrest over execution, forcing Rehm to face proceedings rather than a quiet death. Emotional beat: breaking the cycle of disposal.

chapters.title: The Long Arrest
chapters.summary: Sebastian surrenders publicly on the Hofburg steps, ensuring cameras capture a man choosing accountability over flight. Interrogations begin; he says nothing without counsel — the old rules, finally his own. Emotional beat: dignity in defeat.

chapters.title: Committee of Three
chapters.summary: Months later: hearings across three capitals. Testimony from Marsh, Brandt, and Wren dismantles the program. Some principals escape consequence — the theme refuses neatness. Emotional beat: justice as partial, exhausting, necessary.

chapters.title: Names We Keep
chapters.summary: Mara, legally reconstructed again by choice this time, visits Sebastian in detention. They discuss who they might be without the system defining them. Emotional beat: tenderness earned through ruin.

chapters.title: The Asset Released
chapters.summary: Sebastian walks free, charges narrowed to technicalities, his old life unrecoverable. He declines every offer to consult, guard, or return. Emotional beat: quiet refusal as triumph.

chapters.title: Vienna, One Year Later
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Sebastian runs a small locksmith shop near the Naschmarkt; Wren sends postcards from nowhere; a new listing appears online for a house he once knew — and he simply closes the tab. Emotional beat: peace chosen daily, vigilance kept lightly.
